options: One each under captain and one under first officer seat

questions.text: Operation of QDM (Quick Donning Mask) is: -
options: Insert the palm facing each other, don the QDM and pull the ring
On the overhead panel press the mask man On button and the hood automatically gets donned
Press the push button located near the movable observer seat, don the QDM and pull the quick starter
Squeeze the red grips (harness inflates), remove the mask, don the mask and release the red grips

questions.text: The main cabin exit (e.g. L1 door) can be opened from inside as well as from the outside: -
Which method do we use while evacuating from the cockpit sliding window using the escape ropes?
options: Cockpit sliding windows cannot be opened.

questions.text: How many occupants can be accommodated in the redefined flight deck of freighter aircraft?
How many escape ropes are there in the cockpit?
At what altitude/ time cockpit crew gives the brace commands?
options: 10 seconds or 10 feet prior to the impact
4 minutes or 40 feet prior to the impact
60 seconds or 500 feet prior to the impact
2 minutes or 350 feet prior to the impact

questions.text: When does the captain gives the command for disarming of the slides?
options: Once the aircraft comes to a complete stop
After the aircraft has taken a final turn to the parking bay.
After the seat belt sign goes off

questions.text: What is the method used for arming/disarming the slide?
In a freighter aircraft, Evacuation is conducted through_______________.
After giving verbal warning to the pax if the pax behavior still continues, Lead will issue the RED WARNING CARD, (reads the content) 2 Witness form FSF-14B is filled: -
How many over wing exits are there on A-320 aircraft?
Pre-flight check of Air Liquide PBE: -
options: Check secured in location, ready to use indicator has not changed to BLACK, yellow tamper evident seal intact and expiry is 20 years from the date of manufacturing.
There is no Pre-flight check of the equipment.
Cabin attendants shall conduct the Pre-flight check.
Check secured in location, green ready to use indicator has not changed to RED, yellow tamper evident seal intact and expiry is 10 years from the date of manufacturing.

questions.text: If the Cabin pressure warning light flashes red on the door, the cabin crew shall: -
options: Disarm the slide and then open the door
Not attempt to open the door and call the cockpit crew to inform about the occurrence.

questions.text: Firefighting equipment in the cockpit: -
options: Fire extinguisher, PBE, Gloves and Crash Axe.
Automatic Fire extinguisher, QDM and Gloves.
Fire Extinguisher, Oxygen bottle and PBE

questions.text: During Fire Fighting situation in the Cockpit -command from the cockpit: -

If there is no life threatening condition present in the cabin, aircraft comes to a complete stop and no command from cockpit crew, cabin crew shall call captain: using the following from the handset: -
options: Wait for 10 seconds then make a normal call to the cockpit.

questions.text: During Planned Emergency at 2000ft or 3- 5 min before impact command from the cockpit: -
options: Finish preparation attention crew at station.

questions.text: Duration of PBE (Air Liquide) is: -
To prevent situations leading to ‘Uncertainty of Position’ during Taxi Operations….
options: One pilot should be certain about aircraft position as well as the clearance limit.
Aircraft should continue taxing, stop on active runway and inform ATC.
Crew should maintain positional awareness by using available visual cues such as runway heading and signages.
As a routine, always ask for ‘Follow Me’ vehicle.

questions.text: During departure, when OAT is at or below +3 ⁰C, OET is not permitted due to
options: Insufficient thrust generated by the engines at such low temperatures.
Ice accretion and the required engine acceleration during the ice shedding procedure.
Possibility of fuel imbalance under these conditions.
OET is recommended once De Icing/Anti Icing has been completed.

questions.text: Operational conditions that may prevent OET include high aircraft gross weight. This is because …
options: If the slope is uphill or downhill, it may pose a problem with respect to controlling the aircraft
Excessive jet blast and risk of FOD cannot be avoided
Short radius turns in the direction of the operating engine may not be possible
It would result in fuel imbalance

questions.text: If ATC requests a speed constraint that is not compatible with speed & thrust stabilization at 1000 ft AAL, a later speed and thrust stabilization is acceptable, but not later than
As per Company guidelines, to ensure the aircraft is on correct lateral & vertical path and can accomplish a safe landing, a mental assessment is required to be carried out on all approaches at….
Maximum permitted rate of descent, when aircraft height is below 1000 Ft AAL is
Jeppessen Approach Chart for Hongkong ILS/LOC RWY 07C lists individual Minima for MACG 3.9% and 2.5%. For application of Minima, MACG relates to….
options: Minimum Approach Climb Gradient [one engine inoperative]
Minimum Approach Climb Gradient [all engines operative]
Missed Approach Climb Gradient [one engine inoperative]
Missed Approach Climb Gradient [all engines operative]

questions.text: For optimum fuel tankering, PIC should determine the maximum amount of fuel that can be tankered based on the requirement of the next sector only when…..
options: Actual Zero Fuel Weight is equal to Planned Zero Fuel Weight
Actual Zero Fuel Weight is greater than Planned Zero Fuel Weight
Actual Zero Fuel Weight is below Planned Zero Fuel Weight

questions.text: Ways to avoid additional fuel uplift on every flight include…..
options: Extra fuel should be assessed in terms of quantity and not time
Extra fuel should be assessed in terms of time and not quantity
Extra fuel should be uplifted only if there was an instance when a crew landed with fuel close to MDF

questions.text: Choose the correct statement, with respect to the Depressurization profile graph that has been removed from the FCOM and has been introduced in Company Operations Notice 12
options: The capacity of chemical oxygen generator units is such that, the aircraft must descend and remain below the profile provided in the graph.
The capacity of chemical oxygen generator units is such that, the aircraft must descend and remain above the profile provided in the graph.
The capacity of chemical oxygen generator units is such that, the aircraft must descend and exactly maintain the profile provided in the graph.
The graph is no longer relevant and can be disregarded.

questions.text: Company Drift down & Depressurization Strategies [DD/DP strategies] are required to be established for all route segments with …
In case required, Thrust Ratings for Maximum Take off Thrust and Maximum Climb Thrust can be extracted from the Tables provided in….
Should the Flysmart calculated Flex Temperature be reduced to increase the runway stop margin?
options: Yes, to ensure regulatory requirements are met
Yes, because reducing Flex Temperature would increase Thrust

questions.text: If a SID climb gradient requirement is not achieved, even after changing the climb speed to Green Dot speed, the suggested sequence of modification is….
options: Increase Acceleration Altitude, Thrust Reduction Altitude in that order
Increase Thrust Reduction Altitude, Acceleration Altitude in that order
Increase the Thrust Acceleration/Reduction altitude, as required
Do not accept the SID, if assigned by ATC

questions.text: If Roll oscillations are experienced on A320 aircraft during a Config FULL approach with FINAL APP guidance mode, it is recommended that……
options: PF should transfer controls to PM
PF should ensure that AP is ON

questions.text: If it is perceived that the aircraft will touchdown towards the end of the touchdown zone, the recommended action is …
options: No specific action is recommended if it is an intentional deep landing for minimizing taxi time.
Achieve effective deceleration through timely use of maximum reverse thrust and appropriate braking
Achieve effective deceleration through timely use of maximum reverse thrust and Autobrake Max

questions.text: As regards choice of Landing Configuration in turbulent conditions…..
options: Config FULL is preferred as it meets the ‘handling quality’ criteria
Config 3 is preferred as it meets the ‘handling quality’ criteria
Config FULL is preferred because it provides more energy and less drag
Config FULL or Config 3 can be used as ‘handling quality’ criteria is met satisfactorily in both configurations

questions.text: Company guideline in case Approach Climb Gradient is not met in landing performance with Config 3, states….
options: Compute after increasing VApp [via Vpilot tab on the landing Module input panel]
Select AC Off in EFB Landing module

questions.text: While Going Around in Landing Configuration from low energy state, the initial altitude loss and time required for recovering the initial altitude are significantly increased in case of ...
At Descent Preparation, runway condition is reported as WET and wind shear is expected. Under these conditions, as regards choice of Landing configuration ….
options: CONFIG FULL [to improve performance after touchdown]
CONFIG FULL [to meet handling quality criteria]
CONFIG 3 [provided aircraft performance requirements are met]
Landing should not be attempted Ref. PIN 02K

paper.title: Airbus UPG Performance Question Bank question paper
paper.instructions:
Choose the single best answer for every question.
Mark each answer clearly on the answer sheet.
No reference material is permitted unless the examiner states otherwise.

questions.text: On ECAM Cab. press page, the outflow valve indicator changes to amber if: -
options: It is fully open on the ground
It is fully open in flight
It is not fully open on the ground

questions.text: On ECAM Cab. press page, the cabin altitude indication changes to red when cabin altitude is: -
When you press Extract P/B to OVRD, what happens?
options: Extract fan stops, Air-conditioning air is added for ventilation and avionics ventilation sys goes into Closed Config
Extract fan keeps running, Air-conditioning air is added for ventilation and avionics ventilation sys goes into Closed Config.
Extract fan keeps running, Air-conditioning air is added for ventilation but avionics ventilation sys remains in Open Config.

questions.text: Avionics ventilation system indications may be found on which ECAM page(s)?
options: The in-flight ECAM cruise page and the CAB PRESS pages

questions.text: What is the meaning of LDG ELEV FAULT?
options: Wrong selection of LDG ELEV is made
LDG ELEV selector is moved out of auto without requirement
No FMGS LDG ELEV data is available

questions.text: What is the lateral mode available during TAKE OFF before lift off?
options: RWY mode if ILS tuned corresponding to the departure runway
RWY mode irrespective of an ILS is tuned or not

questions.text: What are the arming conditions for NAV mode on ground?
options: F- PLAN is available and heading preset is selected on FCU and FDs are ON.
F-PLAN is available and no heading preset is selected on FCU and FDs are ON.
F-PLAN is available and NAV aids are tuned manually on RMP and FDs are OFF.

questions.text: When does NAV Mode engage?
options: 30 feet after lift- off provided HDG PRESET is selected
30 feet after lift- off provided HDG PRESET is not selected.

questions.text: What are the Indications when ALPHA-FLOOR Protection is active?
options: The FMA displays green “A FLOOR” surrounded by a flashing amber box and the EWD displays Amber “A FLOOR”.
The FMA displays Amber “A FLOOR” surrounded by a flashing amber box and the EWD displays Amber “A FLOOR”.
The FMA displays Amber “A FLOOR” surrounded by a flashing amber box and the EWD displays Green “A FLOOR”.

questions.text: When is the wind shear protection not available?
What are the indications on the FMA If an engine failure occurs when the soft go-around function is engaged?
options: LVR TOGA flashes on the FMA
MAN TOGA is indicated and FADEC automatically increases the thrust of live engine to TOGA
LVR TOGA flashes on the FMA and FADEC automatically increases the thrust of live engine to TOGA

questions.text: What is required to have “Ground Speed Mini” function possible during Approach?
options: AP + FDs + A/THR+ Managed Speed Function

questions.text: When is Alpha-Floor Protection Inhibited on PW Aircraft?
options: The AP/FD TCAS mode is armed
The aircraft airspeed is below M 0.6
On Single engine when slats/flaps extended

questions.text: What should you do to engage Soft Go-Around Mode?
options: Move both thrust levers to TOGA and then FLX-MCT
Move both thrust levers to TOGA and then CL
In case of OEI, Move the live engine thrust levers to TOGA and then FLX-MCT.

questions.text: Select Correct statement: -
options: Below 150 ft RA, A/THR is less responsive to speed variations.
Below 150 ft RA, A/THR is more responsive to speed variations.
Below 150 ft, A/THR functions in the same manner as at other heights.

questions.text: When does A/THR RETARD mode automatically engage for A321s?
options: It depends upon type of landing whether it is Auto Land or Manual Landing.

questions.text: When the aircraft is in CLB mode and the system predicts that it will miss an altitude constraint: -
options: It will not modify the target speed in an attempt to meet it and may be predicted as missed.
In this case, the flight crew may select an appropriate speed in order to meet the ALT CSTR.
It will modify the target speed in an attempt to meet it.

questions.text: In climb, FMA is showing THR CLB / CLB / NAV. If NAV mode is lost or disengaged, then CLB will revert to: -
options: V/S with a triple click aural warning
OP CLB with a triple click aural warning.
No reversion would take place as a/c is in managed CLB

questions.text: During climb, ALT* means: -
options: A/C is acquiring a selected altitude.
A/THR will be in THR CLB mode after ALT* engagement.

questions.text: During climb, if the FCU target altitude is set below the current a/c altitude: -
options: Pitch mode reverts to V/S and a/c maintains the current rate of climb.

questions.text: During descent, FCU target altitude is set above the current a/c altitude: -
options: Pitch mode reverts to V/S and a/c maintains the current rate of descent.

questions.text: In a managed DES mode, if aircraft is above profile, what is A/THR mode and what does A/P pitch channel control?
options: THR IDLE and speed {IAS} by AP Pitch channel
SPEED and rate of descent by AP Pitch channel
THR IDLE and rate of descent by AP Pitch channel
SPEED and speed {IAS} by AP pitch channel

questions.text: What is the effect on the DES mode, If the NAV mode is lost?
options: No affect at all and DES Mode continues.
DES mode reverts to OP DES mode if above profile
DES Mode reverts to V/S mode always.
DES mode reverts to V/S mode if below profile

questions.text: What speed will the FMGS use in an Expedite climb?
If you have depressed the EXPED push button and want to cancel this function, how could this be accomplished?
options: Push the EXPED push button again.
Pull the altitude or vertical speed knob.
Retard the thrust levers to IDLE.

questions.text: After engine start, “INITIALIZE WEIGHTS” message comes. Gross weight can be inserted on: -
Which of the following data are not computed by FAC?
On the top of your MCDU, it's written "FM 2" in amber, this annunciator means?
options: Indicates that the MCDU has failed
The onside Flight Management (FM) is failed
Indicates that you have received a company message

questions.text: Each FMGC computes its own aircraft position (called the "FM position") from?
options: A MIX IRS position and a computed radio position
A MIX IRS position and a computed radio position, or a GPS position

questions.text: The PACK FLOW controller is set to NORM and yet the ECAM display shows PACK FLOW to be high. How is this possible?
options: As the engines are not running, the PACK FLOW indicators are at the position they were selected to at the last shut down.
As no bleed air is flowing, the PACK FLOW valves are spring loaded to the fully open position.
HI flow is automatically selected regardless of PACK FLOW selector position when air is only being supplied by the APU.
With cold outside air conditions, the PACK FLOW is automatically increased to help increase the cabin temperature.

questions.text: In which case can you get the "MCDU back up navigation”?
Entering a PERF factor of +1.5 means that flight operations have evaluated the aircraft fuel deviation as?
Which page is automatically called up, when the FMGS detects an engine-out condition,?
options: PERF Page for the current flight phase

questions.text: Select the condition where the FMGS fails to automatically call up the PERF page upon an engine failure?
options: If no EOSID (Engine-Out SID) exists in the flight plan
If the flight plan is in "Temporary" status

questions.text: The engine-out REC MAX altitude is computed based on which speed?
What specific condition is assumed by the FMGS when computing the engine-out REC MAX altitude?
If icing conditions are expected during an engine-out, where should the pilot look for REC MAX values?
If a pilot inadvertently activates the approach phase during an engine-out, how can they reactivate the cruise phase?
options: By pressing the PERF key twice
By reselecting the cruise flight level from the PROG page

questions.text: Which of these buses are always powered by batteries?
During flight, when will it be needed to select the BUS TIE pb to OFF?
options: To reset the BUS TIE FALUT.
To reset the BUS TIE contactors.
To segregate both the GENERATOR channels.

questions.text: Ground power is connected to all busses, After engine 1 is started (and Gen 1 is switched ON) what changes will takes place?
options: GEN 1 feeds AC BUS 1, GPU continues to feed AC BUS 2.
GEN 1 feeds AC BUS 1; through BTC 1 & 2 it feeds AC BUS 2 also.
GEN 1 feeds AC BUS 1, AC BUS 2 is not powered.

questions.text: A/c is stationary; both BAT switches are at AUTO; during APU start, where will it’s AC components get power from?
options: At this time, no AC power is needed.
APU start is not possible under these circumstances.

questions.text: IN A FLIGHT, what happens if static inverter fails?
options: AC STAT INV BUS will lose supply immediately
AC STAT INV BUS will be supplied by AC ESS BUS

questions.text: Which buses are supplied by TR1 in normal cases?
options: DC BUS 1, DC BAT BUS and DC ESS BUS
DC BUS 1 and DC BAT BUS
DC BUS 1, DC BAT BUS, DC ESS BUS and DC BUS 2.

questions.text: Name few Electrical components/buses that are not used in normal flight.
options: AC ESS SHED BUS, DC ESS SHED BUS and ESS TR.
ESS TR, Static Inverter and also Emergency Generator.

questions.text: ESS TR operates for: -
What are the points to be observed while disconnecting IDG?
options: Engine is not running; do not press IDG pb switch for more than 3 secs
Engine is not running; press IDG pb switch for a minimum of 3 secs
Engine is running; press IDG pb switch for a minimum of 3 secs
Engine is running; do not press IDG pb switch for more than 3 secs

questions.text: What happens to DC busses when TR 1 fails?
options: All busses are available by auto reconfiguration by using TR 2 and ESS TR
DC BUS 1 DC BAT BUS are lost
DC BAT BUS is lost till 100 KTS

questions.text: Which busses are lost if TR 1, TR 2 have failed?
options: DC BUS 1, DC BAT BUS, DC BUS 2
DC BAT BUS after landing gear extension.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT possible?
options: APU GEN powering AC BUS 1 and the same time GPU powering AC BUS 2
GEN 1 powering both AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2
GEN 1 powering AC BUS 1 and APU GEN powering AC BUS 2
GPU powering AC BUS 1 and GEN 2 powering AC BUS 2.

questions.text: BUS TIE p/b switch is OFF {its normal position is AUTO} and only GEN 1 is available. Which buses are not powered?
What happens to AC ESS BUS in case of AC BUS 2 failure?
options: AC ESS BUS power is not lost as it continues to be supplied from AC BUS 1.
In case of AC BUS 1 failure also, AC ESS BUS has no alternative power.
In case of AC BUS 1 failure also, AC ESS BUS will be supplied by STATIC INVERTOR or emergency generator.

questions.text: In how many ways shall RAT be extended?
options: Automatically when AC BUS1, AC BUS2 had failed and speed is more than 100 kts.
Manually by pressing EMER ELEC PWR MAN ON switch.
Manually by pressing RAT MAN ON switch on Hydraulics panel.

questions.text: What is the function of the GEN 1 LINE push button?
options: When selected OFF, in the avionics compartment, BLOWER and EXTRACT fans stop.
When selected OFF the #1 generator powers all AC busses.
When selected OFF generator # 1 is removed from AC BUS1 but continues to power one fuel pump in each wing.

questions.text: If a break in both engine fire loops occurs within 5 seconds of each other, a _____ will occur.
options: Loop A+B DET FAULT message on ECAM
FIRE DET FAULT message on ECAM

questions.text: If an engine fire is detected, when will the guarded red ENG FIRE push button light extinguish?
options: When the fire warning no longer exists.
When the crew pushes and releases the guarded red ENGINE FIRE pushbutton.
When the crew pushes the red MASTER WARN pushbutton.
When the crew pushes the red MASTER WARN pushbutton and then releases the guarded ENGINE FIRE pushbutton

questions.text: What is indicated by a missing red disc {APU thermal plug} during an exterior preflight?
options: This is normal indication, the red APU thermal plug only appears if the APU halon cylinder is low.
An APU fire agent thermal discharge has occurred.
An external fire discharge has been activated.

questions.text: In case of Avionics Smoke, which page is displayed on S/D?
Illumination of the GEN 1 LINE SMOKE light indicates: -
options: A fire has been detected in the avionics compartment.
A satisfactory test of the avionics compartment smoke detection control unit.
Smoke has been detected in the avionics compartment ventilation duct.
A fire has been detected in the electronics compartment.

questions.text: When does wing tip brakes are active?
options: In case of runaway in slats / flaps
In case of commanded movement in slats / flaps
In case of both SFCC slat channel failure

questions.text: What is the indication if SLAT WTB’S are activated in flight due to slat symmetrical runaway condition?
options: SLATS LOCKED + master warning and CRC

questions.text: What are the flight controls conditions that provide CONFIG warning?
options: SLATS / FLAPS not in T.O. CONFIG.
PITCH TRIM & RUDDER TRIM NOT IN TAKE OFF RANGE

questions.text: What is the bank angle after which positive spiral stability is induced in normal law?
Which statement is correct if one SFCC is inoperative?
options: Flaps and Slats operate at half normal speed
Flaps and slats both operate at normal speed
Slats operate normally, but the flaps operate at half speed

questions.text: What is the effect of ALPHA/ SPEED lock function?
options: It inhibits slats retraction at high angle of attack and / or low speed
Flap operations is not affected by Alpha Speed lock function

questions.text: When does side stick priority CAPT GREEN light illuminate?
options: Whenever Capt’s side stick priority pb is pressed
Whenever F/O side stick priority pb is pressed
When Capt’s side stick priority pb is pressed for more than 40 sec
Whenever Capt’s side stick priority pb is pressed and F/O side stick is not in neutral position

questions.text: Load Alleviation Function in case of gust detection, uses: -
options: Both side Ailerons and No 4 & No 5 spoilers on both wings
Both side Ailerons and No 3 & No 5 spoilers on both wings
All roll spoilers and both ailerons

questions.text: Which computer will control aircraft Pitch functions if all systems are normal?
What happens to bank angle protection if high speed is operative?
options: Bank angle is limited to 45 deg and spiral stability is lost
Bank angle is limited to 40 deg and spiral stability is introduced from 0 deg
Bank angle is limited to 33 deg and spiral stability is introduced from 0 deg

questions.text: In some of the checklists where you have to descent rapidly, SPEED BRAKES FULL is required. In this situation, you have to remember that: -
options: Extension of speed brakes will significantly increase Vls
Angle of attack protection may be activated and, in that situation, speed brakes will retract automatically

questions.text: Where can you check the fuel quantity of each tank?
options: On ECAM LOWER DISPLAY (Fuel page only) (SD)
On both ECAM Upper and Lower Displays. (EWD+SD)

questions.text: Which pumps are fitted with Suction Valves?
options: One wing tank pump on each side.

questions.text: Which pumps keep running throughout the flight?
options: All respective pumps will automatically turn off once fuel in the tank is consumed completely.

questions.text: Which pumps are fitted with pressure relief sequence valves?
Why Gravity feeding is not possible from the centre tank?
options: Because Centre tanks pumps are not fitted with Pressure relief sequence valves
Because Centre tanks pumps are not fitted with Suction Valves
Because Tank Transfer Valves are between outer and inner Tanks.
Because Overpressure protectors between the centre tank and the left inner tanks.

questions.text: How is the Engine LP Valve closed?
options: When the ENG FIRE PUSH pushbutton is pushed or X-FEED pushbutton is selected OPEN.
When the ENG FIRE PUSH pushbutton is pushed or MODE SELECTOR pushbutton in manual.
When the ENG FIRE PUSH pushbutton is pushed or When the engine master switch is turned OFF

questions.text: Which computer has automatic control of the transfer valve?
options: There is no computer system for automatic control of the transfer valve

questions.text: The APU fuel system: -
options: Uses its own dedicated DC powered fuel pump.
Obtains fuel from either centre tank pump.
Obtains fuel from the left fuel manifold via the left side fuel pumps or if needed, the APU fuel pump.
Obtains fuel from the left fuel manifold via the right side fuel pumps.

questions.text: Which computer controls automatic refuelling?
options: No computer but Refuel / Defuel Valves

questions.text: Which unit of Fuel Inerting System produces Oxygen depleted air?
When is the Fuel Tank Inerting System available?
options: From Engine start to Engine shut down

questions.text: When do you get FAULT light in MODE SEL pb-sw?
options: When centre tank has more than 250 kg of fuel and the left- or right-wing tank has less than 5000 kg and the MODE SEL pb-sw is at AUTO.
When centre tank has more than 250 kg of fuel and the left- or right-wing tank has less than 5000 kg.
When centre tank empty and the left- or right-wing tank has less than 5000 kg and the MODE SEL pb-sw is at AUTO.

questions.text: When do you get FAULT light in CTR TK L(R) XFR pb-sw?
options: If the associated wing tank overflows.
If the associated wing tank pump is in operation and the delivery pressure drops.
if MAN mode is selected on the MODE SEL pb-sw.

questions.text: What is the meaning of the ON white light on the CROSS FEED pushbutton?
When will you say that FQI is inaccurate?
options: When two dashes appear across the last two digits of Fuel Quantity Indication
When two dashes appear across the last two digits of Fuel Quantity Indication and quantity turns amber
When two amber crosses appear across the last two digits of Fuel Quantity Indication
When the Fuel Quantity indication is boxed amber.

questions.text: At which fuel quantity is the L/R WING TK LO LVL warning triggered on the ECAM?
After engine shutdown, what are your actions to close the fuel transfer valves?
options: You have to switch the inner tank pumps off.
You have to call maintenance to close the valves.
No action is required. The valves will close automatically during the next refuelling.

questions.text: The message OUTER TK FUEL XFRD appears in the MEMO. What does it mean?
options: It is a reminder to show that at least one transfer valve is open in one wing tank.
Fuel is transferring from the centre tank to the inner tank.
It is a reminder to open the outer tank transfer valve.
Fuel is transferring from inner tank to outer tank

questions.text: An amber line appears across the last two digits of the ECAM FOB indication when: -
options: The wing tank pumps are switched off.
One of the wing tank pumps has failed.

questions.text: On ECAM FUEL page the indication of either wing tank quantity is pulsing. This indicates that: -
options: the related level is 1500 kg higher than the other WING TK level.
the related FUEL QUANTITY indication is inaccurate.
the related level is 1500 kg lower than the other WING TK level.

questions.text: After flying above Flight Level 300 for more than 30 minutes, if gravity fuel feeding procedure is to be applied. What is the ceiling altitude?
Under which condition can the procedure flow in the Technical Notice be carried out without referencing the paper document during flight?
options: As long as the crew are aware of its contents, they can perform the flow immediately to minimize spillage.
It must never be done without referencing the paper document.
Only if authorized by the SVP of Flight Operations via ACARS.
Only if the wing tank fuel quantity is below 5,000 kgs.

questions.text: During cockpit preparation after refueling is over, the crew turns all fuel pumps ON. The First Officer (PM) notices that the fuel quantity in the Left-Wing Tank is increasing even though the tank being full. ECAM Caution has not been triggered. According to Technical Notice 01-04 (“FUEL L(R) WING TK OVERFLOW”), what is the correct action for the crew to take?
options: Wait for 05 minutes to confirm if an auto-logic fault occurs before taking any action.
Crew to carry out immediate actions in the crew action box of the Tech Notice 01-04.
Maintain the affected side pumps OFF and seek assistance from the engineering team.
Before taking any action check the correct position of the affected transfer valve.

questions.text: While taxiing to the holding point, the ECAM alert "FUEL L WING TK OVERFLOW" triggers. The First Officer recalls that the FCOM recommends waiting 5 minutes for fault confirmation before proceeding with the "IF UNSUCCESSFUL" part of the ECAM actions. Why does Technical Notice 01-04 (“FUEL L(R) WING TK OVERFLOW”), direct the crew to carry out the boxed actions immediately instead of waiting?
options: The auto logic of the high-level sensors takes exactly 5 minutes to reset the transfer valve.
During the 5-minute wait period, approximately 300 to 400 kgs of fuel will spill out of the surge tank.
Waiting 5 minutes causes the motive force of the wing fuel pumps to automatically fail.
The FUEL SD page will only show the correct valve position after the 5-minute period has elapsed.

questions.text: During troubleshooting of a wing tank fuel overflow event on the ground, the engineering team explains the system failure to the crew. Which of the following describes the physical root cause of the continuous fuel transfer as detailed in the Technical Notice 01-04 (“FUEL L(R) WING TK OVERFLOW”)?
options: The wing tank high-level sensors failed to detect wet conditions, preventing the automatic opening of the transfer valves.
The fuel cross-feed valve failed in the "OPEN" position, trapping pressurized fuel.
The Center Tank Transfer Valve failed in the "OPEN" position, and motive force remained available because the wing fuel pumps were left "ON".
The center tank transfer pumps failed to shut down automatically after reaching low level.

questions.text: A "FUEL L WING TK OVERFLOW" ECAM triggers while the aircraft is parked at the bay. The Captain commands the "BEFORE ECAM" crew actions. In addition to setting CTR TK L XFR to OFF and FUEL X FEED to ON, what must the crew do with the wing tank pumps, and what is the operational objective of this action?
options: Keep L TK PUMP 1 and 2 ON to pump the excess fuel back into the center tank.
Cycle both L TK PUMP 1 and L TK PUMP 2 to attempt to free a jammed transfer valve.

questions.text:
(a) Given Brake Release Fuel 5400 Kg, Res Fuel 1800 Kg, DOW 42600 Kgs, MZFW 64300 Kgs, MLW 67400 Kgs, MTOW (Perf Limited) 70700 Kg, MTOW (Structural) 79000 Kg. How much extra fuel over 5400 Kg at Brake Release can be carried onboard. (5 marks)
(b) Flight from Delhi to Kolkata. ECAM SPLR FAULT, one SPLR suspected fully extended. FOB at the time of failure 12800 Kg, EFOB destination 7300 Kg. MDF 2700 Kg. What will be the revised EFOB destination and Revised MDF. Can the flight be continued to the original destination. (2,2,1 marks)

solDoc.name: Section B: Extra Fuel & In-Flight Failure

runs.t: Take-off Weight = MZFW + Brake Release Fuel = 64300 + 5400 = 69700 kgs
So, extra fuel can be carried = PLTOW – TOW = 70700 – 69700 = 1000 kgs
Fuel Penalty for ECAM SPLR FAULT, one SPLR suspected fully extended = 55%.
Fuel Penalty = FOB at time of failure – EFOB = (12800 – 7300) x 55% = 3025 kgs
Revised Estimated Fuel on Board at Destination = EFOB – Fuel Penalty = 7300 – 3025 = 4275 kgs
Revised MDF with Fuel Penalty of 55% = 2700 x 1.55 = 4185 kgs
Yes, the flight can be continued to original destination.

(b) Flight from Mumbai to Delhi. ECAM SPLR FAULT, one SPLR suspected fully extended. FOB at failure 12400 kg. EFOB destination 6900 kg. MDF 2800 kg. Determine revised EFOB and revised MDF. Can the flight continue to destination? (2,2,1 marks)

solDoc.name: Section B: Extra Fuel & In-Flight Failure

runs.t: Take-off Weight = MZFW + Brake Release Fuel = 64300 + 5800 = 70100 kgs
So, extra fuel can be carried = PLTOW – TOW = 71700 – 70100 = 1600 kgs
Fuel Penalty for ECAM SPLR FAULT, one SPLR suspected fully extended = 55%.
Fuel Penalty = FOB at time of failure – EFOB = (12400 – 6900) x 55% = 3025 kgs
Revised Estimated Fuel on Board at Destination = EFOB – Fuel Penalty = 6900 – 3025 = 3875 kgs
Revised MDF with Fuel Penalty of 55% = 2800 x 1.55 = 4340 kgs
No, the flight can not be continued to original destination.
